questions.solution_html:
• Mention the divisions of the nervous system in a frog. [K]/[CO2]
  • Ans: The nervous system of a frog is divided into three parts: 1) Central Nervous System
  • (CNS): Consists of brain and spinal cord 2) Perip heral Nervous System (PNS): Includes

questions.question: Explain the life cycle of Thaliacea. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the life cycle of Thaliacea. [U]/[CO1]
  • Ans: Thaliaceans show alternation of generations involving asexual and sexual phases.
  • The life cycle includes two forms: oozooid (asexual form) and blastozooid (sexual form).
  • The oozooid reproduces asexually by budding and produces blastozooids. The
  • blastozooids are sexual forms and produce gametes. After fertilization, a zygote develops
  • into a new oozooid, completing the cycle. (Mention the term Alternation of
  • generation: 1 mark; Explanation: 2 marks)

questions.question: Describe the structure and function of the calcaneum in frogs. / [CO2] [3x6 = 18]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the Structure and function of the calcaneum in frogs. [U]/[CO2]
  • Ans: Calcaneum is a long, elongated bone present in the hind limb of the frog. It is one
  • of the tarsal bones, lying parallel to the astragalus. Function: Helps in jumping and
  • locomotion, by providing leverage to the hind limbs ; Provides support and flexibility to
  • the ankle joint. (Structure: 2 mark; Any 1 function: 1 mark) (Liberal valuation)

questions.question: Describe the major morphological characters used in the subclassification of Chondrichthyes. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the major m orphological characters used in the subclassification of
  • Chondrichthyes. [U]/[CO1]
  • Ans: Subclass Chondrichthyes is divided into Elasmobranchii (sharks and rays) and
  • Holocephali (chimaeras) based on the following morphological features : Gill openings:
  • Elasmobranchii: 5 –7 pairs of separate gill slits, no operculum ; Holocephali: Gill slits
  • covered by an operculum Position of mouth: Elasmobranchii: Ventral mouth ;
  • Holocephali: Terminal mouth Type of scales: Elasmobranchii: Placoid scales present ;
  • Holocephali: Scales absent or reduced Spiracle: Elasmobranchii: Spiracle usually present
  • ;Holocephali: Spiracle absent Tail : Elasmobranchii: Heterocercal tail ; Holocephali:
  • Diphycercal tail ( Any 5 points: 5 marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe parental care in fishes. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe parental care in fishes. [U]/[CO3]
  • Ans: Parental care in fishes refers to the protection and care of eggs and young ones to
  • increase their chances of survival. Types of parental care - Substrate Brooding :
  • Females deposit eggs on substrate and guard them until hatching ; Nest building: Some
  • fishes build nests to lay eggs. Example: Stickleback prepares a nest and guards it. Mouth
  • brooding: Eggs are kept in the mouth of the parent for protection. Example: Tilapia.
  • Brood pouch: In Hippocampus, eggs are kept in a brood pouch of the male until they
  • develop. Significance: Increases survival rate of offspring ; Provides protection from
  • predators and environmental hazards (Definition: 1 mark; Explanation- Any 3 types: 3
  • marks; Significance: 1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Differentiate between the systemic and pulmocutaneous arteries in frogs, mentioning their respective functions. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between the systemic and pulmocutaneous arteries in frog, mentioning
  • their respective functions. [U]/[CO2]
  • Ans: Systemic Arteries: Arise from the truncus arteriosus as a pair of systemic arches;
  • Carry oxygenated blood from the heart to all parts of the body (except lungs and skin);
  • Supply organs like head, trunk and limbs; Function: Distribution of oxygenated blood to
  • body tissues . Pulmocutaneous Arteries: Arise from the truncus arteriosus as
  • pulmocutaneous arches; Carry deoxygenated blood to lungs and skin; Involved in both
  • pulmonary (lungs) and cutaneous (skin) respiration ; Function: Oxygenation of blood
  • through lungs and skin. (Any 3 distinguishing points: 3 marks; Function: 2 marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Distinguish between Eryx johnii and Eryx conicus. / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between Eryx johnii and Eryx conicus. [U]/[CO3]
  • Ans: Eryx johnii is a non-venomous burrowing snake with a uniform reddish-brown body
  • and a very blunt rounded tail that resembles the head, giving a false “two -headed”
  • appearance. Its scales are comparatively smoother and it lives in loose soil where it feeds
  • on small rodents.
  • Eryx conicus is also non -venomous but differs in having brown coloration with dark
  • blotches and rougher keeled scales. Its tail is less rounded than that of E. johnii, and it
  • inhabits sandy or dry areas. (Any 5 distinguishing features: 5 marks)
